newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end quiet session just firmer.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end quiet session just firmer.

text.p: SPI Futures cl 2437 -1 US 30yr cl 7.05 -0.02
10yrbond futs 92.105 -0.060 Gold NY 341.35 Lon fix 342.10
*Stocks closed just firmer in light trade with the stock of gold explorers featuring on the day. Volume 292.1 million, value A$507.8 million, 1,042 stocks traded, 329 steady, 379 up, 334 down.
The Australian share market closed slightly firmer on Monday with the continuing rally on the Wall Street market underpinning the optimistic sentiment for local traders.

The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended 3.4 points up at 2,445.8, after touching an intra-day high of 2,454.5. June share price index futures finished down one point at 2,437, an 8.8 point discount to the index.
The market was mixed for much of the session with National Australia Bank best of the leaders after it suspended its share buyback scheme ahead of its first half results.

"National Bank is a situation where, given just a little bit of uncertainty in the market, most money is comfortable in the bank and its shares are a little bit tighter as a result," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Shaw Stockbroking.
"There is also an expectation that the results might be better than some of the predictions around town," he said.
National Australia Bank shares closed 28.5 cents higher at A$16.794 on turnoevr of 3.65 million shares.
The market had just a 13 point trading range on the day and Spiteri said support for most stock was a carry-over from the agressive buying seen on Friday.
One feature of the session was an impressive performance from a number of exploration companies following the recent release of drilling results.
Carpenter Pacific Resources NL and Ramsgate Resources NL jumped as traders digested Friday's results from the Mt Kare project in Papua New Guinea.
Carpenter shares closed 5.5 cents higher at 43.5 cents, while Ramsgate finished up 2.5 cents at 12 cents.
Arcadia Minerals NL and Sipa Resources NL also climbed higher after well-received drilling results from their Mt Olympus gold prospect in Western Australia.
Arcadia climbed 11 cents to 90 cents, albeit on thin trade, while Sipa also jumped 8 cents to 56 cents.

Fellow explorer Golden Valley Mines NL ended 17 cents higher at 60 cents amid speculation it was close to announcing a new deal on a gold project and rumours of good results from tests of the controversial Busang gold samples being carried out in Australia at the moment.
Golden Valley has an interest in the Muara Atan contract of work which contains part of the Busang deposit.
Rises slightly outnumbered falls, while about a third of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bonds underperformed against the dollar bloc, giving up most of the spread narrowing seen last week as the market took a cautionary stance ahead of the first of this week's major events on Tuesday.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.87 percent, up 0.05 percentage points from Friday's 7.82 percent.
The Australian dollar crept higher over the day as early support prompted scattered short-covering.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the local dollar had drifted back up to US$0.7775/80 from an offshore low around US$0.7725 and up on Friday's late US$0.7750/55.
